narrative:
The model estimates there’s a 50% chance you won’t pass your final year, which is well above the 10% threshold that requires extra support. Because of this, you’ll need to take remedial courses to help you stay on track.

The single biggest reason the model is concerned is that you’ve said you don’t plan to continue your education after high school. Almost every other student who isn’t required to take remedial classes has expressed a clear goal of going to university, so this difference stands out. On a more positive note, you’ve never failed a class before, which works in your favor. Your weekend alcohol use is also very low compared to most students, and that small factor slightly reduces the risk.

To improve your chances, focus first on setting a concrete goal for what comes next—whether that’s further study, training, or work. Even if you’re unsure, simply stating an intention to pursue higher education can shift the outlook. Beyond that, keep up the habits that are already helping you: maintain your strong attendance, avoid repeating past mistakes, and continue making responsible choices about alcohol. The remedial courses will give you extra time and resources to build confidence and close any gaps before the final exams.
